name: Winnetka
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Winnetka, IL 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Winnetka, IL: the Dwyer Park tree lighting with Santa, Winter Wanderland, A Christmas Carol and a Christmas Eve sing on the green.
lede: Winnetka packs much of its Christmas into one early December weekend, with the Dwyer Park tree lighting, Santa at the Community House and the Red Invitation in the shops. The season ends with neighbors singing carols by candlelight on the Village Green on Christmas Eve.
celebrates: Christmas in Winnetka centers on Red Invitation weekend, which the Winnetka-Northfield-Glencoe Chamber of Commerce holds on the second Sunday after Thanksgiving. On the Friday before, the Chamber lights the village tree in Dwyer Park, behind the post office, with carolers, children's choirs, hot chocolate, Santa and a couple of his reindeer. On Saturday morning the Community House Junior Board turns the Community House into Winter Wanderland, a walk through holiday scenes that ends with Santa, and A Christmas Carol plays on its stage that weekend. In December the Winnetka Park District adds gingerbread house decorating, a holiday skate at the ice arena and the Christmas Eve Holiday Sing.
lastyear: In 2025 the Winnetka Holiday Tree Lighting was planned for Friday, December 5, at Dwyer Park, with caroling, Santa and his elves, and hot drinks and treats. The park district's Alvin the Elf's Winter Carnival was planned for the next morning at Skokie School, with carnival games, cookie decorating and reindeer. A Holiday Skating Exhibition and Ugly Sweater Holiday Skate were set for December 13 at the Winnetka Ice Arena, gingerbread house decorating for December 17, and the Holiday Sing on the Village Green for Christmas Eve.
facts: The Chamber says the Winnetka Tree Lighting has been held in downtown Winnetka since 2009, and the Chicago Tribune reported in 2019 that it moved that year from Station Park to Dwyer Park. The Red Invitation is even older. It began in 1976, when one Winnetka retailer held a one-day Sunday sale before the holidays and sent customers a simple red invitation. Neighboring shops joined, and Northfield and Glencoe came in in 2011 and 2021. The Chamber also hangs ornaments on the Dwyer Park tree with the names of the local businesses that sponsor the lighting.
trains: Winnetka has three Metra stations on the Union Pacific North line, which runs from Ogilvie Transportation Center in Chicago to Kenosha: Indian Hill, Winnetka and Hubbard Woods. The Hubbard Woods station, about 80 years old, sits beside the Green Bay Trail, and Metra plans to renovate it. Just south, the CTA Purple Line ends at Linden station in Wilmette, where the Allstate CTA Holiday Train pulls in on its Purple Line runs with Santa waving from his sleigh. Farther afield, the Illinois Railway Museum in Union runs its Happy Holiday Railway, a ride with Santa and his elves.

traditions: Families gather near Elm and Birch for carols, hot chocolate and the 6 pm lighting, and Santa arrives once the tree is lit.
The Community House Junior Board builds holiday scenes that families stroll through on the way to a visit with Santa.
Toby Nicholson and Robert Bowker's version of the Dickens story, with professional actors and North Shore locals, is a Community House holiday tradition.
Since 1976, Winnetka shops have marked their holiday Sunday with clusters of red balloons and seasonal treats.
The Winnetka Ice Arena hosts a holiday skating exhibition and a skate where an ugly sweater gets you in free.
Neighbors bring candles or flashlights to Village Green Park and sing carols together for about 25 minutes.
kidfact: Winnetka's Red Invitation started in 1976 with just one store and one red card. Today you can spot the shops taking part by their clusters of red balloons.
faq: When is the Winnetka tree lighting?

The Winnetka-Northfield-Glencoe Chamber of Commerce holds it at Dwyer Park on the Friday of Red Invitation weekend, which falls on the second Sunday after Thanksgiving. Hot drinks and treats are served from 4:30 to 6:30 pm, the tree lights at 6 pm, and Santa and his elves arrive after the lighting. No registration is needed.
Where is Dwyer Park in Winnetka?

Dwyer Park is in downtown Winnetka near the intersection of Elm and Birch streets, just behind the post office. The Winnetka Park District lists its address as 521 Birch Street. It has been the home of the village tree lighting since 2019, when the Chicago Tribune reported it moved there from Station Park.
Where can kids see Santa in Winnetka?

Santa comes to the Dwyer Park tree lighting after the tree is lit, and he is the last stop on Winter Wanderland, the Community House Junior Board's walk through holiday scenes at 620 Lincoln Avenue. Winter Wanderland includes cookies, hot cocoa and a goodie bag, and every guest, adult or child, needs a ticket.

It is a holiday shopping day on the second Sunday after Thanksgiving that began in 1976 with a single Winnetka retailer. It now covers shops in Winnetka, Northfield and Glencoe, and the Chamber describes the weekend around it as a family tradition with village tree lightings, carolers, children's choirs and visits from Santa and his reindeer.
What is the Winnetka Holiday Sing?

It is a free Christmas Eve sing-along at Village Green Park, 525 Maple Street, hosted by the Winnetka Park District. Families bring candles or flashlights, read from song programs and sing classics from Jingle Bells to Silent Night. It lasts about 25 minutes, and The Record North Shore called it a 29-year tradition in 2024.
